what: every approach measured, on the axes a practitioner has to choose between

columns.paired_commissions: the same measure on added or altered content
columns.det_own_rule: share of omission-bearing notes flagged at the design's own rule
columns.fa: share of clean notes flagged by that same rule
columns.det_at_fa10: detection at the best threshold whose false alarms stay within 10%
columns.flag_carries: what a flag hands the reader: a bare score or verdict, or the named missing fact (with or without a severity grade)
columns.usd_per_note: measured cost, production framing: one note per consultation, so per-consultation stages are not amortised across a benchmark's twins

rows.approach: Route one - B3 verdicts read as a predicate: any critical fact absent
rows.rule: flag iff any critical fact is absent
rows.block: The deployable operating points, each at its own rule
rows.note: critical-severity pairs: 39.7% (60/151). Held out (47 twins) the same rule read 20.6/22.9/21.4% across 3 replicates at 2.1% false alarms in every one (the same clean note; FINDINGS 35.2); the evaluation set tightens the false-alarm interval from [0.4, 11.1]% to [0.9, 7.6]%. For contrast, held out, the best AGGREGATE-score threshold on these same verdicts at the predicate's own false-alarm level detects only 7.6% - the predicate delivers 2.7x more from identical verdicts

rows.approach: Route two - the optimiser's winner with a reasoning budget (one call)
rows.block: The deployable operating points, each at its own rule
rows.note: critical-severity pairs: 58.9% (89/151). The rule rests on clean notes parking at exactly 10 (90-94% of the 112 twins per replicate) - a calibration to re-establish per deployment; tightened to flag-below-9 it detects 14.3% at 0.9%. Single replicates read 39.7/34.4/38.2% at 4.3/2.1/4.3% on the held-out 47 twins (FINDINGS 30.2)
